events.text: A hydroponics tray, a grow lamp wired to a car battery, and behind them a person in a coat made of three other coats. {name} is watering a single tomato with a syringe. It is the only red thing for a hundred metres. 'Careful,' {name} says, not looking up. 'You'll frighten it.' The tomato is the size of a thumb and has, you have a feeling, been named.

outcomes.text: You admire it for the right length of time. {name} cuts it in half with a thumbnail, gives you the bigger half, and eats the other with such grave attention that you look away. 'The vents run behind the pallets,' {name} says, after. 'Your lot would find the rest by smell.'

{name} talks about the tomato for twenty minutes. It is a good tomato. You leave knowing a great deal about tomatoes, with a fistful of hose clamps pressed on you, and feeling, for no reason you can name, a little less alone.
'People leave things,' says {name}, gesturing at a corner like a small and orderly landfill. 'Nobody comes back for them. Seems rude not to sell.'

choices.text: Ask the tomato how it is doing.

outcomes.text: Your Sporeling bends over the tray and makes a small, polite sound. The tomato, you could swear, leans toward it. {name} is delighted, then moved, then slightly jealous. 'Take a cutting,' {name} says thickly. 'Take two.' It turns out a cutting is a coil of grow-line, and a good one.
'Mind the step,' says {name}, to the tomato.

events.text: Every light on this deck has been put out but one. Under it, at a folding table, a person is reading a book with the care of someone defusing it. {name} does not look up. 'You can come in,' {name} says, softly. 'Not with that.' It takes you a moment to understand that {name} means the torch. At the edge of the single pool of light, in the dark beyond it, something shifts and settles, like a coat sliding off a chair.

choices.text: Switch the torch off and sit.

outcomes.text: You sit in the dark, in the circle of the one lamp, and {name} reads aloud. It is a repair manual for a model of pump that has not been built in forty years. It is the best thing you have ever heard. When the chapter ends {name} marks the page. 'The key you want is somewhere with a pump,' {name} says.

You sit. The book is a manual. Something is breathing by your left elbow, slowly, in time with the page. {name} turns a leaf without looking. 'Don't mind the other one,' {name} says. 'He doesn't like visitors.' It does not stay polite for the whole chapter.

{name} closes the book on a finger, stands, and walks out of the circle into the dark. It is not an angry exit. It is the exit of a person who has been asked to leave their own front room. The lamp ticks as it cools.
'Thank you,' says {name}, to the book. The page turns.

events.text: A Concord checkpoint with the lights turned low, and at the one desk still lit a person in a customs lanyard, writing in a ledger that has never once balanced. {name} writes without looking up. 'Fourth door,' {name} says. 'Everyone asks about the first three.' The ledger is open to a page headed GATES, with three columns, and a fourth that someone has added in pencil. The pencil is much newer than the ink.

outcomes.text: 'Core, alloy, a backer,' {name} reads, running a finger down the page, 'and the table. Because the Scrapper Gate has tenants. They have been laying a table for forty years. Bring a kettle.' {name} turns the ledger round so you can read the last line: a signature, a date, and a note in a cramped officer's hand. 'He left it for the next person who came by.'

choices.text: Ask about the vault behind the desk.

outcomes.text: 'Not a vault,' says {name}. 'A cupboard with ambitions.' But the finger goes out, and taps twice on the wall behind the desk, where there is, now you look, a door with a good lock and a small hand-lettered sign: PLEASE DO NOT STEAL.

choices.text: Leave the ledger as you found it.

outcomes.text: {name} writes your departure in the margin. The ink is very black. It will not balance.

events.text: {name} has made a home in the corner of what used to be a mess deck: a bedroll, a stove the size of a hat, a row of bolts on the shelf arranged by size. They look up when your light finds them, and give a small nod, as one tenant to another. 'Quiet tonight,' {name} says. It is the first thing {name} has said in a while, and the voice is rusty with it.

outcomes.text: You stand there a while, listening to the quiet agree with you. {name} warms both hands over the little stove and does not ask you to leave, or to stay. 'East side's safe,' {name} says at last. 'West I wouldn't.'
'It's all small things,' says {name}. 'Small things get you through.'
{name} nods back, and the stove ticks.

events.text: A big brass ship's clock on a bulkhead, and in front of it a person on a stepladder with a key as long as a forearm. {name} winds it with both hands, counts under their breath, and climbs down. Nine more clocks line the passage, all stopped at different hours. 'Mind the third one,' says {name}. 'It is sulking.'

outcomes.text: You take the key. The spring is stiff and the count goes to forty, with {name} nodding at each turn like a teacher. When it ticks, you both listen to it for a while. 'That was the quartermaster's,' says {name}. 'Take the cell from its back. He'd have wanted that.'

'None,' says {name}, delighted. 'But the ninth is the one that was right when they left.' It stopped at 04:10. Somewhere on this ship a door was locked at 04:10, {name} adds, ten minutes after the alarm.
'Time is not for sale,' says {name}. 'The rest is.'
{name} is already counting again, lips moving, before you reach the door.

events.text: A desk in a mail room, a lamp, and a dozen grey sacks slumped against the wall. {name} is reading a letter with a pencil in one hand. A stack of replies stands at the elbow, each in a fresh envelope. 'They never got delivered,' {name} says, not looking up. 'That seemed a poor reason not to answer.'

outcomes.text: 'Whatever they'd have wanted to hear,' says {name}. 'It is mostly weather.' You are given one letter to read. It is mostly weather. It is the kindest thing you have read in a month.
{name} picks an envelope, addressed in a hand so careful it hurts, and pays the postage from a jar: 'If you pass Cordova Station. If you don't, it keeps.' The jar is surprisingly full.
'Undelivered. They were all going somewhere.' {name} taps a sack tag. 'This lot came off the shelf in the cargo bay. There may be more of it, if you want a look at where it came from.'
The pencil moves again before you are out of the room.
